newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sampath grows on quality loans-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Sampath grows on quality loans-analysts.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Sampath Bank Ltd has shown steady growth due to efficiency and prudent lending, market analysts said on Monday.
The blue chip bank recorded net profits of 150.22 million rupees for the six months ending June 30, 1997, a rise of 21.2 percent over the same period in 1996.
"Sampath Bank has again delivered the goods in line with expectations, mostly due to a high rate of efficiency and prudent lending," said Channa Amaratunga, banking analyst at Asia Securities.
The bank has a 55 percent cost to income ratio, which is the best among the four commercial banks listed on the Colombo stock exchange, he added.
"Profits of banks which lend aggressively get hit due to high provisioning," said M.N. Faiz, banking sector analyst at Lanka Securities.
"Because Sampath's lending is not aggressive and high risk, its loan loss provisioning is steady and low," he added.
Kumar Abayanayaka, general manager and chief executive of Sampath Bank, said the bank had worked on improving non-interest incomes.
"Since margins have shrunk by about 200 to 300 basis points, we have begun to concentrate heavily on other sources of non-interest income," he told Reuters.
Interest margins shrank in 1997 after market liquidity improved following a three percent cut in reserve ratios by the Central Bank.
"Non-interest income in the first six months of 1997 was 194 million rupees, compared to 163 million in the same period in 1996," Abayanayaka said.
Analysts have forecast Sampath Bank's net profits for the year to December to rise by 19.6 percent to between 325 and 350 million rupees against 282 million in 1996. ($1= 58.50 rupees)
